content: Murder at Mount Hood | Post Mortem. "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Peter Van Sant discuss the murder of Susan Lane, known as Phoenix, near Oregon's Mount Hood. Grammer wrote the introduction to "The America Opus," a new book celebrating 250 years of American history through archival photos and essays.

author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: The mysterious migration of monarch butterflies. Photographer Jaime Rojo says an iconic 1976 National Geographic cover showing monarch butterflies captivated him, inspiring his own photography. Rojo's new book "Monarchs" chronicles ways we can help save this beloved insect.

title: Second opinion saves career of pro athlete told to amputate leg
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Second opinion saves career of pro athlete told to amputate leg. Doctors said his leg would need to be amputated. Here's how this athlete got back on the field after a rare diagnosis.

author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: More changes are coming for Southwest Airlines, CEO says. Southwest Airlines CEO Bob Jordan shared his plan to bring even more changes to his company and the customer experience. Kris Van Cleave has more.

author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Princess Kate reflects on healing in new documentary: "Cancer does change you". The princess reflects on her cancer journey in the documentary and speaks to others about their experiences.

title: Investigating a dark online subculture where teens glorify killers
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Investigating a dark online subculture where teens glorify killers. A dozen attacks in the last three years, including seven school shootings, were carried out by TCC members, say researchers tracking the group. This Sunday, watch 60 Minutes' six-month investigation into this growing online subculture that idolizes mass shooters.

title: Mamdani's plan to close Rikers Island, revamp NYC jails
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Mamdani's plan to close Rikers Island, revamp NYC jails. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is moving forward with his plan to close Rikers Island and replace it with four smaller jails. Anna Schecter reports.

author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Princess Kate announces she's in remission from cancer. Princess Kate made the announcement on social media after visiting the London hospital where she received treatment.

title: Iowans worry a temporarily halted Army explosion could spread lead, other toxic chemicals
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Iowans worry a temporarily halted Army explosion could spread lead, other toxic chemicals. The U.S. Army wants to detonate aging bomb-making materials, but environmental groups and others warn airborne lead-laced dust could endanger health. Lana Zak reports.

title: How China gets access to American AI chips
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: How China gets access to American AI chips. Jensen Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO following an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. After the Nvidia scandal, China's access to American-made technology and advanced AI chips came under renewed scrutiny. Ramy Inocencio traveled to Southeast Asia to learn more about Chinese usage of American chips.

title: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Trump defends Putin after trilateral with Xi. President Trump, China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin appeared to make little progress in their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China.

author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Denmark says Russia behind plot to kill U.S.-Ukrainian citizen on its soil. Officials said police thwarted the attempt when they arrested three men with links to the Danish criminal underworld in a car before the rapper Kyivstoner was set to perform at a concert north of Copenhagen in late September.

title: Britain's Princess Kate climbs 3 mountains in 24 hours for charity
author: Staff Wire Correspondent
content: Britain's Princess Kate climbs 3 mountains in 24 hours for charity. The challenge was undertaken to raise awareness for a charity she has been involved with since her own cancer treatment.

author: The Associated Press
content: Mexico detains top cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro,' setting off violence. Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
author: Imogen Foulkes
content: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules. U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

title: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks
author: Scott Simon
content: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks. As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks. NPR's Scott Simon talks with Phillips O'Brien of St. Andrew's University.

title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
author: The Associated Press
content: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI. A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.

title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
author: The Associated Press
content: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in. Efforts to establish rules for AI-powered killer robots and drones have run aground. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva ended Saturday with an agreement to extend discussions for two more years.

title: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine
author: Eleanor Beardsley
content: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine. On the outskirts of Kyiv, one family prepares for the fifth winter of war against Russia -- stockpiling food and fuel and trying to maintain as much a sense of normalcy as possible.

title: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results
author: Franco Ordoñez
content: Trump touts meeting with Xi and Putin but offers few results. At a White House press conference Friday, Trump offered little in actual results of the meetings, beyond a joint statement on unity over some issues.

author: Brittney Melton
content: Dems aim to block Iran war funding. And, Army delays lead azide detonation in Iowa. Congress needs to pass a funding measure to avoid a shutdown next month, providing Dems an opportunity to leverage power. And, the Army says waiting to detonate lead azide could become dangerous.

author: Leila Fadel

author: The Associated Press
content: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties. A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences.

author: Katie McQue
content: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?. Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested.

author: The Associated Press
content: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year. AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market.

author: Cooper Katz McKim

title: Critics are worried about Anthropic's influence after first day of public trading
author: Shannon Bond
content: Critics are worried about Anthropic's influence after first day of public trading. Anthropic's initial public offering was a success for shareholders, including its founders. But there were also protests about whether the company can be a responsible steward of AI technology.

author: Rafael Nam
content: How exactly did Trump get so rich on crypto? We explain. President Trump has made billions of dollars in his second term — most of it in cryptocurrencies. Democrats are vowing to probe his businesses as they gear up to take over Congress next year.

title: AI giant Anthropic's shares pop in debut after blockbuster IPO

content: AI giant Anthropic's shares pop in debut after blockbuster IPO. Shares in the AI juggernaut Anthropic are now trading on the stock market. They debuted Thursday, after a record-breaking IPO.

author: Scott Detrow
content: Tech stocks end the week on a down note, despite Anthropic's mega-IPO. The stock market is ending the week down despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO and a strong Nvidia earnings report, largely thanks to investor jitters about the future of AI.

title: Machine Gods: Anthropic's early days
author: Kevin Roose
content: Machine Gods: Anthropic's early days. In the wake of AI giant Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, Machine Gods hosts Kevin Roose and Casey Newton look back on the early days of the company, when less than 200 workers in a cramped office obsessed over AI safety and viewed business as an afterthought.

title: Experts say powering data centers uses more water than cooling them
author: Alex Hager
content: Experts say powering data centers uses more water than cooling them. Fears about data center water use are especially acute in Arizona. But keeping servers cool uses a lot less water than generating the electricity for which data centers are so thirsty.

title: AI models are propelling rapid growth and revealing vulnerabilities
author: Jenna McLaughlin
content: AI models are propelling rapid growth and revealing vulnerabilities. AI models are exposing the internet's longstanding insecurity, driving rapid change and technical outages.

title: Business opportunity or security threat? Nvidia case raises questions about China
author: Greg Myre
content: Business opportunity or security threat? Nvidia case raises questions about China. The Nvidia case illustrates the friction between Silicon Valley, which wants to sell high-tech products to China, and the national security community, which aims to restrict U.S. tech to China.
